newsitem.title: CHINA: Qantas seeks short cut to Europe via China.
newsitem.headline: Qantas seeks short cut to Europe via China.

text.p: Qantas Airways is hoping to win permission from Beijing for new air routes over China that will significantly cut flight times to Europe and allow increased payload, a Qantas official told Reuters.

Senior Chinese government officials travelled to Sydney in May to meet Qantas executives and Australian government officials to discuss new routings over southwest China and the northern Himalayas. The Australians are awaiting a decision, he added.

The Australian flag carrier has 14 passenger flights a week between Australia and the UK, via either Singapore or Bangkok, as well as services to Rome and Frankfurt. But traditional routings over the Bay of Bengal have become an increasing bottleneck for Qantas and other carriers, the official said.
Shorter flight times and reduced fuel burn will allow extra cargo payload.

Qantas is also keen to exploit satellite-based navigation equipment fitted to its Boeing 747-400 long-haul fleet. CNS/ATM (Communication Navigation Surveillance/Air Traffic Management) technology allows pilots to choose shorter routes and optimum altitudes by communicating with air traffic controllers in remote regions via data messages instead of by traditional radio transmissions.

Analysts said Europe-bound airlines from Hong Kong, such as Cathay Pacific Airways Limited and British Airways, have enjoyed shorter journey times and increased belly cargo loads since China allowed a new short cut over the northwestern city of Urumqi late last year.

Up to 90 minutes has been shaved off typical flight times between Hong Kong and London and with a Boeing 747 burning almost seven tonnes of fuel per hour analysts said airlines such as Cathay have been able to dramatically increase revenue because of the shorter route.
